# Comparison between the variant and collapse modes

```{python}
import pandas as pd
import matrix as mt

RESULTS = {"collapse": "../result/eris_validation", "variant": "../result/eris_validation_variant"}
ASSEMBLIES = {"complete": "Complete genome (FASTA)", "simulated": "Simulated GFA", "real": "Real-reads GFA"}
TRUTH = {"complete": mt.GT_COMPLETE, "simulated": mt.GT_CHROMOSOME, "real": mt.GT_COMPLETE}


def read_loci(report):
    """One row per IS name: its copies, from the number of loci (variant) or their copy_number (collapse)."""
    loci = pd.read_csv(report, sep="\t").drop_duplicates("locus_id")
    loci["copies"] = loci["copy_number"].fillna(1) if "copy_number" in loci else 1
    loci = loci.assign(target=loci["target"].str.split(",")).explode("target")  # a locus can hold several IS
    loci["name"] = loci["target"].map(mt.is_name)
    by_name = loci.groupby("name")["copies"].sum().reset_index()
    by_name["group"] = by_name["name"].map(mt.is_group)
    return by_name


metrics = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{path}/metrics.tsv", sep="\t").assign(mode=mode) for mode, path in RESULTS.items()])
side = metrics[(metrics["dimension"] == "side") & (metrics["class"] == "both")]
relations = side.set_index(["assembly_type", "mode"])[["TP", "FN", "TP_calls", "FP", "precision", "recall", "f1"]]

loci = pd.DataFrame([{"assembly_type": a, "mode": mode,
                      **mt.precision_recall_gfa(mt.read_truth(bed, exclude=["ISSen10"]),
                                                read_loci(f"{path}/EC958/{a}/eris/h3_report.tsv"))[0]}
                     for a, bed in TRUTH.items() for mode, path in RESULTS.items()])
loci = loci.set_index(["assembly_type", "mode"])[["TP", "FN", "FP", "precision", "recall", "f1"]]

table = pd.concat({"IS–CDS relations": relations, "IS loci": loci}, axis=1).round(2)
table = table.reindex(list(ASSEMBLIES), level=0).rename(index=ASSEMBLIES)
table.index.names = ["assembly", "mode"]
table
```

## IS–CDS relations by status and reason

Truth relations are TP or FN (`wrong_side`, `wrong_IS`, `not_found`); eris's false nearest flanks are FP (`unplaceable`, `wrong_side`, `wrong_IS`, `not_in_truth`). Every FN also has a miss cause (`budget`, `not_reported`, `not_called`).

```{python}
rows = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"{path}/EC958/{a}/relations.tsv", sep="\t").assign(assembly=name, mode=mode)
                  for mode, path in RESULTS.items() for a, name in ASSEMBLIES.items()], ignore_index=True)
rows["reason"] = rows["reason"].fillna("–")
columns = pd.MultiIndex.from_product([list(ASSEMBLIES.values()), list(RESULTS)])
pd.crosstab([rows["status"], rows["reason"]], [rows["assembly"], rows["mode"]]).reindex(columns=columns, fill_value=0)
```

FN by miss cause:

```{python}
fn = rows[rows["status"] == "FN"]
pd.crosstab(fn["miss_cause"], [fn["assembly"], fn["mode"]]).reindex(columns=columns, fill_value=0)
```


- Variant mode reports every path through a collapsed repeat, not one consensus per repeat 
- **Higher recall**: a copy whose flanks collapse mode left out can still appear as a variant path. Every TP variant mode gains was a `not_reported` miss in collapse mode: 12 on simulated and 18 on real. They’re mostly multi-copy IS such as ISEc12 (4 and 5), IS26, ISEc23, IS200 and ISEc52.
- **Lower precision**: the graph allows combinations that don’t exist in the genome. Each of those paths becomes a locus, and its nearest genes become FP calls. That’s why the extra FPs are almost all not_in_truth (29 → 44 on real) and come from multi-copy IS: ISEc8 (+3), IS30 (+3), ISEc23, ISEc12, IS1A and IS3411 (+2 each).
- Precision counts each call: one extra path through a repeat adds two new nearest-flank calls, one per side. So every wrong path costs precision twice.

# Comparing pyfgs and real FGS

- I run FGS only in complete genome and found there are 5620 genes that are similar between pyfgs, genome 

FragGeneScan 1.32 was run on the complete genome outside eris, with the `complete` model in both its modes: `-w 0` (fragments, what eris uses: `GeneFinder(model=Model.Complete, whole_genome=False)`) and `-w 1` (whole genome). Genes are compared by replicon, start, end and strand.

```{python}
def read_genes(gff):
    genes = pd.read_csv(gff, sep="\t", comment="#", header=None, usecols=[0, 2, 3, 4, 6],
                        names=["replicon", "type", "start", "end", "strand"])
    genes = genes[genes["type"] == "CDS"]
    return set(genes[["replicon", "start", "end", "strand"]].itertuples(index=False, name=None))


GENE_CALLS = {"pyfgs (eris, w0)": "../result/eris_validation/EC958/complete/eris/h3_assembly.gff",
              "FGS 1.32 w0": "../result/fraggenescan_complete/EC958_fgs_w0.gff",
              "FGS 1.32 w1": "../result/fraggenescan_complete/EC958_fgs.gff"}
calls = {name: read_genes(path) for name, path in GENE_CALLS.items()}
REPLICONS = {"HG941718.1": "chromosome", "HG941719.1": "pEC958", "HG941720.1": "pEC958B"}
pd.DataFrame({name: {"genes": len(g), **{label: sum(x[0] == r for x in g) for r, label in REPLICONS.items()}}
              for name, g in calls.items()}).T
```

```{python}
def stop(gene):
    replicon, start, end, strand = gene
    return replicon, end if strand == "+" else start, strand


names = list(calls)
pd.DataFrame([{"first": a, "second": b, "identical": len(calls[a] & calls[b]),
               "same stop": len({stop(g) for g in calls[a]} & {stop(g) for g in calls[b]}),
               "only first (by stop)": len({stop(g) for g in calls[a]} - {stop(g) for g in calls[b]}),
               "only second (by stop)": len({stop(g) for g in calls[b]} - {stop(g) for g in calls[a]})}
              for i, a in enumerate(names) for b in names[i + 1:]])
```

- With the same setting (`-w 0`), pyfgs and FragGeneScan agree on 5,620 genes exactly. pyfgs alone has 5 genes, all 66 bp on the minus strand; FragGeneScan alone has 49 full-sized genes (368–2,828 bp) that no pyfgs gene overlaps.
- The mode matters more than the program: `-w 0` calls about 390 more genes than `-w 1`, and about 880 shared genes have a different start.
- None of the 49 FragGeneScan-only genes is behind a `not_called` miss on the complete genome: for 10 of the 15, both callers have a gene there that does not pass the match test (mostly partial or pseudo truth CDS); for the other 5, neither calls one.

# New IS-CDS validation independent of gene quality

The curated score matches eris's pyfgs genes to RefSeq CDS, so gene-calling errors (a spurious short ORF, a gene that misses the 50% overlap, a CDS pyfgs never called) count against eris. The new **assignment score** asks only: *did eris attach its own genes to the right side of the right IS?* The answer key is built from the truth IS BED and eris's own called genes, and flanks are matched by gene ID, so gene calling cannot cause a mismatch.

## Pipeline

```{=html}
<svg width="100%" viewBox="0 0 700 90" role="img" style="max-width:760px;font-family:inherit">
<title>Assignment score pipeline</title>
<defs><marker id="ar" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto"><path d="M2 1L8 5L2 9" fill="none" stroke="#5F5E5A" stroke-width="1.5"/></marker></defs>
<g font-size="12.5" text-anchor="middle">
<rect x="6" y="16" width="126" height="56" rx="6" fill="#F1EFE8" stroke="#888780" stroke-width="0.6"/><text x="69" y="40" fill="#2C2C2A" font-weight="500">Run eris</text><text x="69" y="58" fill="#5F5E5A" font-size="11">hops 3 and 20</text>
<rect x="146" y="16" width="126" height="56" rx="6" fill="#F1EFE8" stroke="#888780" stroke-width="0.6"/><text x="209" y="40" fill="#2C2C2A" font-weight="500">Place genes</text><text x="209" y="58" fill="#5F5E5A" font-size="11">all called, on reference</text>
<rect x="286" y="16" width="126" height="56" rx="6" fill="#FAEEDA" stroke="#854F0B" stroke-width="0.6"/><text x="349" y="40" fill="#633806" font-weight="500">Answer key</text><text x="349" y="58" fill="#854F0B" font-size="11">nearest gene per side</text>
<rect x="426" y="16" width="126" height="56" rx="6" fill="#E1F5EE" stroke="#0F6E56" stroke-width="0.6"/><text x="489" y="40" fill="#085041" font-weight="500">Detected IS</text><text x="489" y="58" fill="#0F6E56" font-size="11">from _loci.fasta</text>
<rect x="566" y="16" width="126" height="56" rx="6" fill="#F1EFE8" stroke="#888780" stroke-width="0.6"/><text x="629" y="40" fill="#2C2C2A" font-weight="500">Score by gene ID</text><text x="629" y="58" fill="#5F5E5A" font-size="11">precision, recall</text>
</g>
<g stroke="#5F5E5A" stroke-width="1" marker-end="url(#ar)"><line x1="133" y1="44" x2="144" y2="44"/><line x1="273" y1="44" x2="284" y2="44"/><line x1="413" y1="44" x2="424" y2="44"/><line x1="553" y1="44" x2="564" y2="44"/></g>
</svg>
```

1. **Run eris** on each assembly twice: hops 3 is scored; hops 20 only tells a `budget` miss from `not_reported`.
2. **Place every gene eris called** (CDS and pseudogenes in `_assembly.gff`) on the reference.
3. **Answer key**: for each IS copy in the BED and each side (read along the BED strand), the nearest placed eris gene is *expected*. Tied genes, e.g. identical IS26 transposases, form one relation that any of them finds.
4. **Detected IS**: the new `_loci.fasta` header gives each locus's position (`contig:start-end strand=` or the contig path when stitched). A locus is placed with 1 kb of context to tell identical copies apart; a copy no locus covers is `undetected`.
5. **Score by gene ID**: precision over eris's nearest flanks (FP: `unplaceable`, `overcall`, `wrong_side`, `wrong_IS`, `not_nearest_gene`); recall over expected relations (FN: `undetected`, `wrong_side`, `wrong_IS`, `not_found`). The headline leaves the IS-detection errors (`overcall`, `undetected`) out.

## Results

```{python}
RULES = ["any_copy", "own_copy"]
assigned = pd.concat([pd.read_csv(f"../result/eris_validation/EC958/{a}/assignment/{r}/metrics.tsv", sep="\t")
                      for a in ASSEMBLIES for r in RULES])
assigned = assigned[assigned["class"] == "both"].rename(columns={"edge_rule": "rule"})
assigned = assigned.set_index(["assembly_type", "rule"])[["precision", "recall", "f1", "overcall", "undetected"]]

curated = pd.read_csv("../result/eris_validation/metrics.tsv", sep="\t")
curated = curated[(curated["dimension"] == "side") & (curated["class"] == "both")]
curated = curated.set_index("assembly_type")[["precision", "recall", "f1"]]
curated = curated.reindex(assigned.index.get_level_values(0)).set_axis(assigned.index)

table = pd.concat({"Assignment score": assigned, "Curated score": curated}, axis=1).round(3)
table = table.reindex(list(ASSEMBLIES), level=0).rename(index=ASSEMBLIES)
table.index.names = ["assembly", "rule"]
table
```

- Most of what the curated score counts against eris is gene calling: on the complete genome eris's side assignment reaches F1 0.94–0.96 against 0.70.
- The 4 `overcall` FPs are two ISEc49 loci with no ISEc49 copy in the BED.
- Remaining errors on the complete genome: IS609 flanks on the opposite side to the BED (its family has no inverted repeats, so the orientation may be a convention difference); ISSen10 and ISSen1, short partial copies eris does not detect; and BED `IS26_2` (HG941719.1:37108–38748, 1,640 bp, twice IS26's length), which eris calls ISEcp1. **To check: is this copy really ISEcp1?**

## `any_copy` vs `own_copy`

Every IS contains its own transposase, which is never its own flank. The two rules differ only for a gene inside a *neighbouring* IS: `any_copy` leaves out genes inside any IS copy, `own_copy` only those inside the copy being judged. eris itself walks outward and reports every gene it meets, so at two adjacent IS it reports the neighbour's transposase.

- This pattern (IS30/IS600, ISEc9/IS5, IS26/ISEcp1) is the whole difference on the complete genome: 16 FP under `any_copy`, 11 under `own_copy`.
- Which rule is right is a biology question: should a neighbouring IS's transposase count as "the gene next to this IS"? Decide by reading these rows, not by the higher score.
